profile.headline: SRE Software Engineer at Google
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
Building reliable Software at scale.

Ph.D. in Computer Science with experience in Algorithm Design, Data Visualization, and Geometric Data Processing.

positions.title: Senior Software Developer
positions.description:
Worked on map visualization engine/framework that draws on multi-core technology for real-time rendering of large geospatial datasets. This framework integrates with existing GIS solutions at Lakes, including legacy software. The project involved coding in C++ for various platforms, including .NET and Win32, and the use of various technologies, such as COM, Direct2D, and GDI+.

Implemented a distributed rendering service for Web maps, using the Open Street Map dataset, as well as a customized Web Tile Service to provide access to the rendered imagery. The latter was done using C# MVC technologies for the server side as well as Javascript for the front end.

Developed solutions to integrate Web mapping services with Enterprise Resource Planning products. Implemented in Python and Javascript.

positions.title: Post-doctoral fellow
positions.description:
My post-doctoral fellowship at Lakes consisted of researching and developing algorithms for geometric processing and graphical visualization of air pollution. Most significantly, I lead the development of the 3D interface of Lakes Web products.

Some of the algorithmic problems I tackled during this time period included contouring of geographic data in 2D and 3D, boolean operations on polygons, smoothing of polygons and polytopes, topological composition, compression of geometric data, and computation of various types of triangulated meshes.

For these projects I have used the following technologies: C++, WebGL, Flash/Stage3D, Java3D, Javascript, C#, WCF, and ASP .NET.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
I took various Research Assistant positions during my PhD in both the School of Computing and the Department of Geography at Queen's.

At the School of Computing I worked on research problems related to my thesis: "Problems on Geometric Graphs with Applications to Wireless Networks". This research led to the publication of 5 papers in scientific journals and conference proceedings. I also worked on other problems of geometric nature in collaboration with scientists from around the globe.

At the Department of Geography I worked on the implementation of algorithms for geostatistical analysis, pollution data visualization, and a set of academic tools.

positions.title: Teaching Fellow
positions.description: Lectured for a course on numerical analysis and algorithms (30 students).

positions.title: Instructor
positions.description: Lectured courses on Discrete Mathematics and Computer Programming. Also run tutorials for Design and Analysis of Algorithms.

positions.title: Lead Programmer
positions.description:
Led a team of 7 programmers for the development of various geographic information systems (GIS) tools. The main task consisted in developing an ESRI equivalent GIS for the internal use of CADIC S.A., Spain..

Among other tools, I coded a Web Service based client-server solution for distributed querying and modification of geospatial data. The development was based on C# and .NET 1.1.

honors.title: ESRI Award to the Best Scientific Paper in GIS.
Industrial Research and Development Fellowship
honors.description: Awarded to selected fellow post-doctoral researchers, with the purpose of conducting research at an industrial partner's facility.
